candidate.answerReason: There are 2 vowel orders and 60 distinguishable consonant orders, giving 120 arrangements.

methods.label: Account for the identical T's
methods.explanation:
The vowels \(O\) and \(E\) must occupy the first two positions. They can appear as \(OE\) or \(EO\), giving \(2\) choices.

The last five positions contain \(C,N,T,S,T\). Temporarily label the two T's as \(T_1\) and \(T_2\). The five distinct letters then have
\[
5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot2\cdot1=120
\]
orders. Every distinguishable consonant arrangement occurs exactly twice in this count, because exchanging the labels on its two T's does not change the actual word. Thus there are \(120/2=60\) consonant orders.

Every valid rearrangement has exactly one vowel order and one distinguishable consonant order, so the total is
\[
2\cdot60=\boxed{120},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
